what: Whether tools/knowledge_vault.find_notes resolves a vault note from the name LB says out loud, and how much of the gap two candidate resolvers close.
why: find_notes is the free path. One hit and LB gets his own words back for nothing; zero hits and the turn either dies or escalates to a paid agent that then has to search. Every miss here is a wrong answer or a Gemini request.
how: python media/scripts/measure_vault_recall.py — runs the live find_notes and two candidate resolvers over the same phrase set against the real vault. Nothing in tools/ is modified; the candidates are re-implemented in the measure script, the same convention measure_kicad_parser.py uses.

conditions.resolver: tools/knowledge_vault.find_notes — exact stem, then substring stem, then >=2 significant-word overlap
conditions.candidate_alnum: split a letter/digit boundary into two words, in the query and in the filename
conditions.candidate_title: alnum, plus let a note be matched by its own first H1 heading and by an `aliases:` frontmatter list

headline: On what LB has actually said, the resolver is already 6/6 and is NOT the bottleneck. Every failure in this table is synthetic.
caveats: THE REAL SET IS THIN AND THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE HERE. Six real phrases, of which only THREE are positive note lookups, and all three point at the same note (english research question). The other three correctly resolve to nothing. Three lookups against one note is not a fixture set, and no threshold-shaped decision should be taken from it.

This is the trap config/oddball.toml documents for the wake threshold, arriving in a second place: a fixture set with no marginal cases certifies whatever is already shipped. The synthetic rows were written by Claude, not by LB, and they are the ones that fail — which is exactly what you would expect from invented fixtures whether or not the resolver has a problem.

The two course notes were generated by tools/syllabus_to_vault.py on 2026-08-29 and are one day old. There is no log evidence of LB reaching for them by voice yet — so 'EEGR 105' failing is a predicted failure, not an observed one. It is cheap to fix and worth fixing before the term makes it expensive, but it has not cost anything yet.
Phrases are scored on WHICH note comes back, not on what is then said about it. A resolver hit followed by a bad read is scored RESOLVED here.

REAL phrases are transcribed from data/oddball.log and the capture filenames in captures/, Whisper's own errors preserved. They are what base.en produced, which is what the resolver actually has to survive.
next: Record real attempts at the course notes and at the robot arm note, put them in PHRASES marked REAL, and re-run. The durable fix is the phrase set, not the resolver — same conclusion the wake threshold reached.
